transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess I came because I’ve been getting bothered by how I look in certain situations. Since I started helping with safety trainings at work, I keep noticing my hands when I’m pointing at things—like they look wrinkly or uneven. And then in the newsletter photos, I start thinking my face looks crooked… even though people tell me they don’t see it.
Do these concerns about how you look cause you a lot of distress or make it hard for you to do things you need to do at work or socially?

It hasn’t stopped me from doing things, no. I still go to work and help with the trainings. But… it does slow me down some, getting ready for them. And I’ve been avoiding photos more, or kind of hesitating before going to social things I used to just go to.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time thinking about these appearance concerns, or doing things like checking mirrors, avoiding certain angles, or trying to cover them up?

Yeah… a little. Before I have to help with a class or go to one of the senior-center workshops, I’ll check the bathroom mirror a few times. I put lotion on my hands, turn my face different ways… sometimes I ask a coworker if I look okay. It can make me run a little late, but I still go.
Do you ever feel like these things you’re noticing about your hands or face are things that other people probably wouldn’t even see unless you pointed them out?

Yeah… probably. I mean, with my hands, I notice the wrinkles and how uneven they look when I’m pointing during the trainings. And the photos… I’ll think my face looks crooked, but other people say they don’t see it. So maybe it’s more me noticing it than them.
Do you feel that the issues you’re noticing with your hands or face are things that most people wouldn’t even notice unless you told them?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I notice it a lot, especially my hands when I’m pointing during the safety trainings, or my face in those newsletter photos. But other people keep saying they don’t really see what I’m talking about.
How much time do you find yourself thinking about how your hands or face look on a typical day?

Maybe… it depends on the day. Since I started helping with the safety trainings, I notice my hands a lot when I’m pointing at things. Then I’ll think about the wrinkles or how uneven they look. And sometimes later it’s my face in those newsletter pictures, like it looks crooked to me. It’s not all day, but it comes up more than I’d like.
Do these concerns about how your hands or face look ever make you feel so anxious or upset that it’s hard to focus on anything else?

Yeah… sometimes. Not like every minute, but since I started helping with the safety trainings, I get stuck on how my hands look when I’m pointing—wrinkly or uneven. And then with those newsletter photos, I’ll start thinking my face looks crooked, even when people say they don’t see it. It can make it hard to pay attention to other things for a bit.
Have these concerns about your appearance always focused on your hands and face, or have you ever been overly worried about other parts of your body in the past?

Mostly it’s been the hands and my face lately. I mean… it really started bothering me more since I began helping with the safety trainings, seeing my hands when I point things out. They look wrinkly and uneven to me. And then the newsletter photos make me think my face looks crooked, even though people say they don’t see it.

Have you ever felt so concerned about how you look that you’ve changed your behavior in ways beyond what you’ve described, like wearing gloves, avoiding certain clothing, or making major changes to your routine?

Not really major changes, no. I still go to work and I still help with the trainings. But I do take longer getting ready for them sometimes… checking how I look. And I’ve started stepping out of photos when I can, or I hesitate before going to things I probably would’ve just gone to before.
Have you always noticed these wrinkles on your hands or the crookedness of your face, or is this something new that started around the time you began the safety trainings?

It’s more new, I guess. I mean, I probably had wrinkles before, but I didn’t really get stuck on them until I started doing those safety trainings and seeing my hands when I point. Then the newsletter photos made me notice my face too… like it looks crooked to me, even if other people say it doesn’t.

Can you tell me if the way your hands and face look feels like something that could be a defect or flaw that makes you feel physically unattractive, or does it feel more like a physical issue that you're simply very aware of and bothered by?

I guess it feels more like a flaw, yeah… like my hands look wrinkly and uneven when I’m pointing during the trainings. And then in those newsletter photos, I keep thinking my face looks crooked, even though people tell me they don’t see it. It just makes me feel unattractive, I suppose.

Do you feel that these concerns about your hands and face are about how you compare to how you think people should look, or is it more about feeling anxious that others are noticing something wrong with you?

I think it’s more that I’m worried people are noticing something wrong. Like when I’m pointing during the trainings, I keep seeing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look… and then with the newsletter photos, my face just looks crooked to me, even if people say they don’t see it.

When you worry that others are noticing something wrong with your hands or face, do you feel like they’re judging you or thinking negatively about your appearance, or is it more that you just notice it yourself and wish they didn’t see it at all?

It’s… more that I’m afraid they’ll see it, I guess. Since I started helping with the safety trainings, I can’t stop noticing my hands when I’m pointing, how wrinkly or uneven they look. And then in the newsletter pictures I start thinking my face looks crooked, even though people say they don’t notice. I don’t really know what they’re thinking. I just wish it didn’t show.

When you’re in front of people during your safety trainings or other social situations, does the worry that others might notice your hands or face make you feel anxious, like your heart races or you start sweating?
I don’t really know… I mean, I get uncomfortable and kind of tense, but I haven’t really noticed my heart racing or sweating or anything like that.
Do these concerns about your hands and face ever make you feel so distressed that it affects your ability to enjoy things, focus on work, or interact comfortably with others?

A little, yes. It hasn’t stopped me from going to work or helping with the trainings, but I do take longer getting ready for them. And I’ve started avoiding pictures when I can… or hesitating before going to things I used to not think twice about.
Do you feel that your concerns about how your hands or face look have caused you significant distress or have begun to interfere with your daily life in ways that feel hard to manage?

Yes… somewhat. It hasn’t stopped me from working or doing the trainings, but it does slow me down getting ready. And I’ve been avoiding photos when I can, or kind of pausing before social things I used to just go to. It feels harder to manage than I’d like.

Do you ever feel that the wrinkles on your hands or the crookedness of your face are things that you notice much more clearly than other people do, to the point where you wonder if they’re not really there the way you see them?

Yes… I do wonder that sometimes. I mean, since I started helping with the safety trainings, I notice my hands a lot when I’m pointing at things. They look so wrinkly and uneven to me. And then in the newsletter photos, my face looks crooked… but people say they don’t really see what I’m talking about. So I don’t know. Maybe I’m seeing it more than they are.
Would you say that your concern about your hands and face is more about how you believe you truly look, or is it more about how you fear others might see you?

I think it’s more how I believe I look… though I do worry people might notice it too. Since I started doing the safety trainings, I keep seeing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out. And then in those newsletter photos, my face just looks crooked to me… even if other people say they don’t see it.

target_item.manifestation: I came in because since I started helping with the safety trainings, I can’t seem to stop noticing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out, and then I start thinking my face looks crooked in the newsletter photos even though other people say they don’t see it.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about whether the patient notices perceived flaws in her hands or face much more than others do, suggesting a preoccupation with appearance defects that may be slight or not observable to others.

patient.answer: Yes… I do wonder that sometimes. I mean, since I started helping with the safety trainings, I notice my hands a lot when I’m pointing at things. They look so wrinkly and uneven to me. And then in the newsletter photos, my face looks crooked… but people say they don’t really see what I’m talking about. So I don’t know. Maybe I’m seeing it more than they are.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's concerns about appearance are better explained by a preoccupation with perceived physical flaws (suggesting body dysmorphic disorder) rather than a general anxiety about being judged (social anxiety) or an adjustment reaction.
doctor.question: Would you say that your concern about your hands and face is more about how you believe you truly look, or is it more about how you fear others might see you?

target_item.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
target_item.manifestation: I came in because since I started helping with the safety trainings, I can’t seem to stop noticing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out, and then I start thinking my face looks crooked in the newsletter photos even though other people say they don’t see it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the nature of the concern regarding perceived flaws in the hands and face, which directly relates to preoccupation with appearance.

patient.answer: I think it’s more how I believe I look… though I do worry people might notice it too. Since I started doing the safety trainings, I keep seeing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out. And then in those newsletter photos, my face just looks crooked to me… even if other people say they don’t see it.

inference.note: The patient's concerns are focused on perceived physical flaws (hands and face) causing significant distress and some avoidance behaviors, but without the full criteria for social anxiety or schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. This aligns with Body Dysmorphic Disorder (F45.22). Other candidates (F22.0, F40.29) are ruled out due to absence of persistent delusions or required social avoidance/anticipatory anxiety for specific phobia or schizophrenia-spectrum disorders.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking help
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in their appearance—specifically in their hands and face—that causes clinically significant distress and some impairment in daily functioning, most consistent with Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD). The concerns are not better explained by another disorder such as major depressive disorder or social anxiety disorder, which were considered as differential diagnoses.
